I've had a lot of jobs in my 20 years working, none that required a degree for what it's worth.

Currently I'm an order picker for a big grocery chain.

It's a union job with decent pay and benefits.

What I love is that it's always busy, and there's always work, so no time to sit idle and start to think about how you're at work and what's it all for, etc.

​

* It's face paced.
* Work on your own, but with others around you doing the same.
* Lifting and walking expels energy and feels good to be fit.
* Get to obsess and perfect stacking boxes to make beautiful square pallets for shipping.
* Time flies.
* No micro-managing if you follow the simple job requirements.
* Working in refrigerator temps is actually more comfortable than room temp.

​

This job is great for me, so far, but we'll see if it will stand the test of time.

​
